text: Amoxicillin belongs to which WHO AWaRe group?
explanation:
Amoxicillin (penicillin, ATC J01CA04) is an Access antibiotic: wide activity against common pathogens with low resistance potential.

Reference: WHO AWaRe classification 2023 (WHO-MHP-HPS-EML-2023.04 xlsx), sheet 'AWaRe classification 2023'; Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021), Annex 2 (Access list).

text: Flucloxacillin is classified in which AWaRe group?
explanation:
Flucloxacillin is an Access penicillin, listed as a therapeutic alternative to cloxacillin.

Reference: WHO AWaRe classification 2023 (WHO-MHP-HPS-EML-2023.04 xlsx), sheet 'Access'; Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021), Annex 2 (Access list, no. 14).

text: Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid (co-amoxiclav) is best described as:

options.A: A penicillin in the Watch group
options.B: A cephalosporin in the Access group
options.C: A beta-lactam/beta-lactamase-inhibitor combination in the Reserve group
options.D: A beta-lactam/beta-lactamase-inhibitor combination in the Access group

explanation:
Co-amoxiclav (J01CR02) is a beta-lactam/beta-lactamase-inhibitor combination and is an Access antibiotic.

Reference: WHO AWaRe classification 2023 (WHO-MHP-HPS-EML-2023.04 xlsx), sheet 'AWaRe classification 2023'; Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021), Annex 2 (Access list, no. 3).

text: Which AWaRe group should be protected as 'last-resort' options for confirmed or suspected multidrug-resistant infections?
explanation:
Reserve antibiotics (e.g. linezolid, colistin, tigecycline) are kept for MDR organisms when alternatives have failed or are unsuitable.

Reference: WHO Practical Toolkit: AMS Programmes in Health-care Facilities in LMICs (2019), Figure 11 (Section 4.7); Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021), Annex 2.

text: Which is a brand name of Amoxicillin + Clavulanic Acid combination preparation?
In which of the following scenarios is Co-amoxiclav (Amoxicillin + Clavulanate) clinically preferred over Amoxicillin alone?

options.A: First-line therapy for mild community-acquired pneumonia without comorbidities
options.B: Empiric treatment of acute bacterial sinusitis when beta-lactamase producing pathogens (H. influenzae / M. catarrhalis) are suspected
options.D: Prophylaxis for uncomplicated acute viral cough

explanation: Reference: WHO AWaRe Book 2022 (Chapter 7, p. 71): Addition of clavulanic acid restores activity against beta-lactamase producing organisms like H. influenzae and M. catarrhalis.

text: Which antibacterial fixed-dose combination is scientifically justified and listed in the national and WHO Essential Medicines Lists?
explanation:
The STG names amoxicillin-clavulanic acid as a justified FDC; cefuroxime-clavulanic acid is called unjustified polypharmacy.

Reference: Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021), Section 2.4; WHO AWaRe classification 2023 (WHO-MHP-HPS-EML-2023.04 xlsx), sheet 'Not recommended'.

text: When selecting empiric therapy for acute bacterial rhinosinusitis where beta-lactamase producing pathogens (Haemophilus influenzae or Moraxella catarrhalis) are suspected, why is Amoxicillin-Clavulanate (Co-amoxiclav) clinically preferred over Amoxicillin alone?

options.A: The addition of clavulanic acid inhibits beta-lactamase enzymes, successfully restoring and broadening antibacterial activity against resistant strains.
options.B: Clavulanic acid acts as a potent antitussive agent that suppresses uncomplicated viral upper respiratory cough.
options.C: Co-amoxiclav belongs to the Reserve group, making it the required first-line agent for mild outpatient pharyngitis.
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for renal function dose adjustments in elderly patients.

explanation:
The addition of clavulanic acid (a beta-lactamase inhibitor) protects amoxicillin from degradation by beta-lactamase-producing organisms, rendering it clinically effective against resistant respiratory pathogens like H. influenzae.

Reference: WHO AWaRe Antibiotic Book 2022 (Chapter 7, p. 71); Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021).

text: Why is it essential to instruct patients/caregivers to refrigerate oral reconstitutions of Co-amoxiclav (Amoxicillin + Clavulanic acid) suspension in warm tropical climates like Bangladesh?

options.A: Amoxicillin precipitates rapidly at room temperature
options.B: Clavulanic acid rapidly degrades at ambient temperatures
options.D: Refrigeration changes the color to signal active dose

explanation:
WHO AWaRe Book 2022 (p. 45, 61): Clavulanic acid is thermally unstable and rapidly metabolizes/degrades in high ambient temperatures.

Reference: National AMR Surveillance in Bangladesh 2016-2023, 'Antibiotic use' summary and Figure 58 (AWaRe distribution).

text: What is the standard adult dose of linezolid (IV or oral) with normal renal function?
explanation:
Adults receive linezolid 600 mg q12h by IV or oral route.

Reference: WHO AWaRe Antibiotic Book, Web Annex (Infographics), p.150 (Linezolid); Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021), Table 6.1 (Reserve: linezolid 600 mg IV 12 hourly).

text: Which statement about linezolid dosing in renal impairment is correct?

options.A: Reduce the dose by 50% if CrCl is below 50 mL/min
options.C: Give the same dose but only once daily
options.D: It is contraindicated in renal impairment

explanation:
Linezolid needs no renal dose adjustment, which is why it is an option in MRSA infection with severe renal impairment.

Reference: WHO AWaRe Antibiotic Book, Web Annex (Infographics), p.150 (Linezolid).

text: Which statement about the route of administration of linezolid is correct?

options.A: It must be given IV for at least 7 days before oral switch
options.B: Oral absorption is poor so only IV is effective
options.C: Oral treatment can be started from the beginning because oral bioavailability is high
options.D: The oral form is only for children

explanation:
High oral bioavailability allows initiation with oral therapy as an alternative to IV (tablets 400/600 mg; IV 2 mg/mL).

Reference: WHO AWaRe Antibiotic Book, Web Annex (Infographics), p.150 (Linezolid).

text: Why Penicillin manufacturers require dedicated Penicillin Manufacturing Unit?
Which oral amoxicillin dose is listed for adults with mild-to-moderate community-acquired pneumonia in the WHO AWaRe book?
explanation:
AWaRe book lists amoxicillin 1 g q8h orally for mild-to-moderate CAP (normal renal function).

Reference: WHO AWaRe Antibiotic Book, Web Annex (Infographics), Community-acquired pneumonia, pp.39-40.

text: Pregnancy category of Amoxicillin + Clavulanic Acid is
In the Bangladesh STG, what is the IV co-amoxiclav dose for severe adult pneumonia?
explanation:
Severe CAP: co-amoxiclav 1.2 g IV 8-hourly plus clarithromycin 500 mg IV 12-hourly (AWaRe book: 1 g + 200 mg IV q8h).

Reference: Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021), Table 6.1 (Pneumonia, adult); WHO AWaRe Antibiotic Book, Web Annex (Infographics), CAP pp.39-42.

text: What oral flucloxacillin dose does the Bangladesh STG recommend for superficial soft tissue infection/cellulitis in adults?
explanation:
Flucloxacillin 500 mg orally 6-hourly (7 days), an Access, narrow-spectrum anti-staphylococcal choice.

Reference: Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021), Table 13.7 (Soft tissue infection/Cellulitis).

text: Which of the following conditions is the main clinical indication for prescribing oral or intravenous Flucloxacillin?

options.A: Suspected Staphylococcal skin and soft tissue infections (e.g., boils, impetigo, cellulitis)
options.B: Typhoid fever caused by Salmonella Typhi
options.C: Urinary tract infection caused by Escherichia coli

explanation: Reference: Bangladesh STG 2021 (p. 56, 59) & WHO AWaRe Book: Flucloxacillin is an isoxazolyl penicillin specifically targeted against Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA).

text: A 40-year-old adult patient is prescribed oral Co-amoxiclav (Amoxicillin + Clavulanic Acid) for a moderate soft tissue infection. What is the standard adult oral dose and frequency?
explanation:
Bangladesh STG 2021 (p. 25, 59) & WHO AWaRe Guidelines: Standard adult oral Co-amoxiclav is 500/125 mg TDS (8-hourly) or 875/125 mg BD (12-hourly).

Reference: Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021), Table 8.1 (Acute Endocarditis).

text: Which antibiotic is the preferred treatment for infected bite wounds, and why?

options.A: Amoxicillin alone, because it is cheapest
options.C: Co-amoxiclav, because it covers anaerobes as well as skin flora
options.D: Linezolid, because it covers all bite pathogens

explanation:
Bite wounds involve oral anaerobes, so co-amoxiclav 500/125 mg q8h is preferred (flucloxacillin and amoxicillin alone lack full cover).

Reference: WHO AWaRe Antibiotic Book, Web Annex (Infographics), Wound and bite-related infections, pp.57-58.

text: For a mild, non-bite skin infection, which choice is preferred from a stewardship view over co-amoxiclav?
explanation:
Cloxacillin/flucloxacillin (and cefalexin) have narrower spectra than co-amoxiclav and work well in mild SSTI, so they are preferred.

Reference: WHO AWaRe Antibiotic Book, Web Annex (Infographics), Wound infections pp.57-58 and SSTI pp.49-52; WHO AWaRe classification 2023 (WHO-MHP-HPS-EML-2023.04 xlsx), flucloxacillin = therapeutic alternative to cloxacillin.

text: Why is Clavulanic Acid combined with Amoxicillin in Co-amoxiclav preparations?

options.A: To reduce the renal excretion of amoxicillin
options.B: To inhibit beta-lactamase enzymes produced by bacteria, restoring amoxicillin's activity
options.D: To eliminate the need for refrigeration of oral suspensions

explanation: WHO AWaRe Guidelines & Bangladesh STG 2021: Clavulanic acid is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects amoxicillin from degradation by beta-lactamase-producing organisms.

text: Which is an appropriate use of linezolid?

options.D: MRSA infection in a patient with vancomycin hypersensitivity

explanation:
Targeted use: MRSA with severe renal impairment, vancomycin hypersensitivity, or need for oral therapy; VRE/VRSA; XDR-TB. Using it for simple OPD infections is irrational.

Reference: WHO AWaRe Antibiotic Book, Web Annex (Infographics), p.150 (Targeted treatment); National AMR Surveillance in Bangladesh 2016-2023, Reserve drug use in OPD (Table 14).

text: A ward patient was started on IV co-amoxiclav and is improving at 48-72 hours. What do stewardship principles advise?

options.B: Review the therapy and switch IV to oral or narrow the spectrum if culture and clinical status allow

explanation:
Hospital antibiotics should be reviewed at 48-72 hours, with early IV-to-oral switch and de-escalation.

Reference: WHO Practical Toolkit: AMS Programmes in Health-care Facilities in LMICs (2019), AMS competencies table (PDF p.71).

text: A 35-year-old male presents with severe dental abscess with facial swelling, trismus (inability to open mouth), and high fever (38.5°C). After performing surgical drainage/extraction, which oral antibiotic option is appropriate according to AWaRe guidelines?
explanation:
WHO AWaRe Book 2022 (Chapter 8, p. 93): For spreading dental infections with systemic features, Access group penicillins (Amoxicillin or Phenoxymethylpenicillin) are first-line adjuncts to surgical drainage.

Reference: Bangladesh STG on Antibiotic Use in Common Infectious Diseases, v1.0 (DGHS, 2021), Table 8.1; National AMR Surveillance in Bangladesh 2016-2023, Conclusions (MRSA 70%).
